title: Scoped PRD: SAML delegated authorization + customer key escrow evidence playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This PRD defines the scoped requirements, scope changes, and the operational evidence checklist for delivering SAML-based delegated authorization, role mapping for RBAC, and a customer key escrow + attestation flow for Private/VPC deployments. The goal is to create an actionable playbook that operations, release engineers, and compliance can use to validate a customer's readiness and to provide a reproducible sign-off path for KMS/HSM-backed key custody and SSO federation. Includes acceptance criteria, test scenarios, and links to artifacts for verification.
background_and_problem_statement: Customers deploying Redwood Private demand auditable SSO/RBAC integration with the ability to onboard customer-managed keys (CMEK) or escrowed keys for disaster recovery. Current onboarding is ad hoc: missing clear evidence artifacts for security teams, inconsistent SAML attribute mappings, and unclear operator steps for HSM import/export and attestation. This ticket scopes the minimum viable evidence set and the operator playbook to ensure repeatable sign-off.
scope_change_notes: Originally this ticket covered only SAML SSO + RBAC mapping. During Product/Legal review we expanded scope to include a targetted key-escrow attestation flow and a minimal HSM import verification step to satisfy enterprise auditors. Non-goals: full key escrow UI, automated escrow key rotation scheduler (deferred to later cycle).
acceptance_criteria: SAML integration: test tenant successfully completes SAML handshake with IdP and asserts required attributes (name, email, groups) in two IdP providers (Okta, Azure AD) using provided attribute map templates
RBAC mapping: at least three role-mapping policies (read-only, operator, admin) applied and validated via API keys and SSO login, with documented sample assertions and audit entries
Audit logs: access and key-management events are emitted to the private audit log stream, with tamper-evidence metadata and retention policy documented
KMS/HSM escrow: operator-run import produces a signed import receipt (attestation) that includes key fingerprint, import timestamp, operator identity, and HSM certificate chain
Evidence package: for a sample customer onboard, produce a zip containing SAML metadata exchange logs, role mapping matrix, audit log snippet, key import receipt, and the operator playbook checklist
Playbook verified: runbook executed end-to-end by Solutions Engineer in staging with recorded session and post-run checklist, no unresolved blockers
Security review: security sign-off obtained and issues closed in tracker (security_review_required = true)
signoff_checklist: Operator runbook created in docs repo: docs/private/onboard-key-escrow.md
Runbook verification: Solutions Eng recorded session uploaded to Drive and shared with Security
GH PR: infra changes merged for audit event schema (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4128)
SAML templates: idp-attribute-maps added for Okta and AAD (templates/okta-aad-maps.yaml)
HSM attestation produced and verified by Security Team (attestation ID A-2025-0219-07)
Compliance evidence pack attached to ticket and to customer onboarding artifact store
Final sign-off: Product, Security, Solutions Eng, and Legal approvals recorded
test_scenarios: Happy path SAML: engineer performs IdP metadata exchange and user signs in, group claims map to 'operator' role, request emits audit event 'saml.login' with group claim
RBAC negative test: user with missing group claim denied elevated API access and receives clear error code and audit log entry
Key import verification: import key via HSM operator flow, validate import receipt signature and compare fingerprint to uploaded manifest
Audit retention: simulate retention query and ensure the audit entry for key import is queryable and immutable for the configured window
decisions: Decision 1: Use signed import receipts for escrow evidence instead of relying solely on HSM operator logs to simplify auditor review
Decision 2: Attribute mapping will be schema-driven with a small set of templates for Okta and Azure AD to reduce onboarding variability
Decision 3: Defer automated key rotation and escrow UI to future release; provide operator CLI for import/export in this scope
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: IdP claim variability across enterprise customers — Mitigation: provide attribute map templates and a quick diagnostic tool to validate IdP assertions
Risk: HSM vendor differences mean import receipts can vary — Mitigation: require canonical fingerprinting and a standard receipt wrapper verified by our attestation cert
Risk: Audit data volume in Private may affect retention costs — Mitigation: allow configurable retention and sample-based evidence extraction for sign-off

notes: This ticket is intended to create a repeatable, low-friction path for Security and Compliance teams to accept Private deployments where customers bring their own keys or require escrow. Keep artifacts minimal and auditor-friendly. If successful, this playbook will be templated into the Private onboarding flow.
